title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure
summary: Management locks (CanNotDelete or ReadOnly) can be applied at subscription, resource group or resource scope and are inherited by child resources. They block deletion or modification regardless of a user's RBAC role, and creating or removing them needs Microsoft.Authorization/locks permissions.

title: Enforce a minimum required version of TLS for requests to a storage account
summary: The storage account property minimumTlsVersion sets the oldest TLS version clients may use. Microsoft recommends TLS 1.2 and describes using Azure Policy to audit or enforce it, and logs to find clients still using older versions before changing the setting.

title: Find and delete unattached Azure managed disks
summary: Managed disks keep billing after the VM they belonged to is deleted. The guidance shows how to find disks whose state is Unattached and delete them after confirming they hold nothing needed; a snapshot first is a cheap rollback.

title: Overview of Azure Resource Graph
summary: Azure Resource Graph lets you query resource inventory across subscriptions with a subset of KQL. It is read-only, returns current resource properties, and only shows resources the caller has at least read access to.

title: Overview of Azure Policy
summary: Azure Policy evaluates resources against rules and can audit, deny or remediate them (for example with DeployIfNotExists). It is the preventive counterpart to detection: policy stops drift, while an audit finds drift that already exists.

title: Azure built-in roles: Reader
summary: The built-in Reader role can view all resources but cannot make changes. Granting an auditing identity only Reader enforces read-only behavior at the platform level rather than relying on application code.
